d8158c74-f3c4-4d9e-9430-cdd2b6e78da6.name: Bachelor of Commerce (Applied)
d8158c74-f3c4-4d9e-9430-cdd2b6e78da6.description:
Box Hill Institute's Bachelor of Commerce (Applied), CRICOS 116460H, is a 3 year, 24 subject degree (144 points: 12 core, 8 major and 4 elective subjects) covering accounting, finance, management, marketing, business ethics, law, economics and communications. Classes are timetabled face to face on weekdays, and the final year includes a 6 to 7 week workplace internship from which students deliver and present a critical business project.

The institute's own course page frames the degree around small group teaching rather than large lecture theatres, with one on one support from teaching staff who bring practical industry experience. Box Hill highlights past student outcomes including a Commerce student who won the Victorian International Student of the Year (Higher Education) award and the Premier's International Student of the Year award.

Graduates are expected to leave with a broad, coherent body of business knowledge, critical analysis and synthesis skills, and the communication skills to present ideas clearly and independently, positioning them for accounting, financial advisory and economics roles.
d8158c74-f3c4-4d9e-9430-cdd2b6e78da6.curriculum: 24 subjects across 3 years (144 points): 12 core subjects (72 points) covering accounting, finance, management, marketing, business ethics and law; 8 major subjects (48 points); and 4 elective subjects (24 points). The final year includes a 6 to 7 week workplace internship culminating in a critical business project.
d8158c74-f3c4-4d9e-9430-cdd2b6e78da6.admission_requirements: International students must have completed an Australian Year 12 or international equivalent with a pass (Box Hill Institute's own published entry requirement for this course). Box Hill Institute only accepts enrolments from international students who are 18 years of age or above at the time of course commencement.
d8158c74-f3c4-4d9e-9430-cdd2b6e78da6.english_requirements: A minimum IELTS overall score of 6.0 (Academic) with no band less than 5.5, or an approved equivalent test. Applicants wanting to strengthen their English first can take Box Hill's own English for Academic Purposes 1 and 2 courses before progressing.

eac06b00-c008-433f-9a44-fe66bc522a14.name: Bachelor of Community Services
eac06b00-c008-433f-9a44-fe66bc522a14.description:
Box Hill Institute's Bachelor of Community Services, CRICOS 082590E, is a 3 year, 24 subject degree built around service delivery in the community services sector: students develop a broad understanding of the principles and theories underlying the field, analyse traditional welfare models against contemporary theoretical perspectives, and study cultural safety with a strong Indigenous focus.

The course combines classroom study with practical placement and applied learning subjects, giving students real world experience in and around the community services sector alongside a cohort of fellow students they're encouraged to learn from and support. Teaching covers applicable legislation and regulation, and builds decision making and communication strategies for community services work.

The institute's own learning outcomes emphasise professional communication, critical evaluation of community services theory, self management, teamwork across diverse disciplines, and analysing community development within a global context that takes cultural and socioeconomic diversity into account, preparing graduates for roles such as child protection practitioner, alcohol and other drugs worker, crisis intervention worker or residential care officer.
eac06b00-c008-433f-9a44-fe66bc522a14.curriculum: 24 subjects across 3 years, combining classroom study of community services principles, welfare models and legislation with practical placement and applied learning subjects that provide direct sector experience.
eac06b00-c008-433f-9a44-fe66bc522a14.admission_requirements: International students must have completed an Australian Year 12 or international equivalent with a pass. Applicants may be asked to complete an interview covering their suitability for and understanding of the course, and must hold or be able to hold a current National Police Records Check and Working with Children Check. Box Hill Institute only accepts enrolments from international students who are 18 years of age or above at the time of course commencement.
eac06b00-c008-433f-9a44-fe66bc522a14.english_requirements: A minimum IELTS overall score of 6.5 (Academic) with no band less than 6.0, or a minimum TOEFL score of 83 (internet based, with each section no less than 20 for listening, 19 for reading, 24 for writing and 20 for speaking), or an approved equivalent test.

955d2606-aa8e-4184-bb32-acf22395da4b.name: Bachelor of Design
955d2606-aa8e-4184-bb32-acf22395da4b.description:
The Bachelor of Design, CRICOS 111000K, is Box Hill Institute's TEQSA accredited award (renewal date 13 May 2029) covering the fashion side of its design portfolio. Box Hill currently markets the degree as two distinct majors sharing the same course code and CRICOS registration: Bachelor of Design (Fashion Design) and Bachelor of Design (Fashion Enterprise), each with its own dedicated live course page. There is no separately marketed plain "Bachelor of Design" page; the base award is delivered through these two majors.

The Fashion Design major covers the complete fashion product lifecycle from concept development through patternmaking, garment construction and product development to responsible fashion practice, while the Fashion Enterprise major covers the same lifecycle from a market research, trend forecasting, buying and merchandising angle, aimed at students building brands and bringing products to market rather than designing garments themselves. Both majors run 28 units over 3 years (12 core units, plus either 14 major and 2 electives for Fashion Design or 10 major and 6 electives for Fashion Enterprise), include an 80 hour industry internship, and involve live industry projects with Australian fashion brands such as Cotton On Group, Sportsgirl, Sussan Group, Jockey Australia and Peter Alexander.

Box Hill is a proud supporter of Seamless, Australia's national clothing stewardship scheme, and both majors build toward a more responsible, circular fashion industry. Graduates of either stream leave with a professional portfolio and industry experience, aimed at roles from fashion designer and costume designer to fashion buyer, trend forecaster and fashion entrepreneur.
955d2606-aa8e-4184-bb32-acf22395da4b.curriculum: 28 units over 3 years. Fashion Design major: 12 core units, 14 major units, 2 elective units. Fashion Enterprise major: 12 core units, 10 major units, 6 elective units. Both majors include an 80 hour industry internship and live industry projects with Australian fashion brands.
955d2606-aa8e-4184-bb32-acf22395da4b.admission_requirements: International students must have completed an Australian Year 12 or international equivalent with a pass. The Fashion Design major requires a portfolio of at least 8 images demonstrating creativity, artwork, fashion illustrations and concept development. Box Hill Institute only accepts enrolments from international students who are 18 years of age or above at the time of course commencement.
955d2606-aa8e-4184-bb32-acf22395da4b.english_requirements: A minimum IELTS overall score of 6.0 (Academic) with no band less than 5.5, or an approved equivalent test, for both the Fashion Design and Fashion Enterprise majors.

ff0a4e94-2af2-4d3a-81ab-bc2d6ce0cc0f.name: Bachelor of Early Childhood Education
ff0a4e94-2af2-4d3a-81ab-bc2d6ce0cc0f.description:
Box Hill Institute's Bachelor of Early Childhood Education, CRICOS 075815G, is a 4 year degree comprising 28 core subjects and 4 practicum subjects, with a total of 80 days of supervised placement. Core subjects pair 30 hours of face to face lecture, tutorial and workshop time with around 5 hours of online activity, and class attendance is compulsory.

The course covers the philosophies, principles and practices of early childhood teaching, integrating core discipline areas of language and literacy, mathematics, the arts, science, and health and wellbeing into play based learning programs. Students build leadership and management capability for diverse early childhood service types, alongside child development, child and family centred practice, legal and regulatory compliance, inclusive environments, and early childhood leadership.

The program is recognised by the Australian Children's Education and Care Quality Authority (ACECQA) and meets Victorian Institute of Teaching (VIT) standards for Early Childhood Teacher registration, so graduates are required to register with VIT as an Early Childhood Teacher on completion, qualifying them to teach across preschools, kindergartens, early learning centres and long day care settings.
ff0a4e94-2af2-4d3a-81ab-bc2d6ce0cc0f.curriculum: 28 core subjects plus 4 practicum subjects over 4 years, totalling 80 days of supervised placement. Each core subject pairs 30 hours of face to face class time with about 5 hours of online activity; attendance is compulsory.
ff0a4e94-2af2-4d3a-81ab-bc2d6ce0cc0f.admission_requirements: International students must have completed an Australian Senior Secondary Certificate (including Mathematics) or international equivalent with a pass in a final year secondary mathematics unit, or completion of a tertiary entrance mathematics equivalency course (TEMEC). Applicants must complete an individual face to face selection interview of approximately 30 minutes, hold or be able to hold a current National Police Records Check and Working with Children Check, and have competent computer skills for online tutorials and StudentWeb submissions. Box Hill Institute only accepts enrolments from international students who are 18 years of age or above at the time of course commencement.
ff0a4e94-2af2-4d3a-81ab-bc2d6ce0cc0f.english_requirements: At least one of: Academic IELTS overall 6.5 with no band less than 6.0 (or approved equivalent); an Australian Senior Secondary Certificate (VCE or equivalent) score of at least 30 in English (EAL) or 25 in another VCE English group of studies at Units 3 and 4; or completion of an Australian Advanced Diploma or Diploma in Early Childhood Education and Care within the last 12 months.

b22ac442-cdd4-4151-8b63-173afcec4008.name: Bachelor of Hospitality Management
b22ac442-cdd4-4151-8b63-173afcec4008.description:
Box Hill Institute's Bachelor of Hospitality Management, CRICOS 116459A, is a 3 year, 24 subject (144 point) degree aimed at students planning to manage large hospitality operations rather than only work the floor of them. Subjects cover accounting, marketing, business and hospitality law, workplace communications, strategic project management, contemporary issues in hospitality, and contemporary human resources management, with a work based hospitality management project giving students a real venue or business problem to solve.

The institute's own course page emphasises small class sizes and one on one lecturer support over a typical large university business school model. Students who have completed an accredited diploma or advanced diploma in tourism, events or hospitality may receive credit towards the degree.

Graduates are expected to leave with a broad, coherent body of hospitality management knowledge, critical analysis and synthesis skills, and clear independent communication skills, aimed at roles such as function manager, account manager, sales and marketing manager, human resource manager, small business operator or event manager.
b22ac442-cdd4-4151-8b63-173afcec4008.curriculum: 24 subjects (144 points) over 3 years, covering accounting, marketing, business and hospitality law, workplace communications, strategic project management, contemporary issues in hospitality and human resources management, plus a work based hospitality management project.
b22ac442-cdd4-4151-8b63-173afcec4008.admission_requirements: International students must have completed an Australian Year 12 or international equivalent with a pass. Relevant employment experience in industry and/or other undergraduate studies will be considered for subject exemptions. Box Hill Institute only accepts enrolments from international students who are 18 years of age or above at the time of course commencement.
b22ac442-cdd4-4151-8b63-173afcec4008.english_requirements: A minimum IELTS overall score of 6.0 (Academic) with no band less than 5.5, or an approved equivalent test.

dc599cb7-371c-4709-bcbc-bf8b983b2467.name: Bachelor of Information Technology
dc599cb7-371c-4709-bcbc-bf8b983b2467.description:
Box Hill Institute's Bachelor of Information Technology, CRICOS 107931A, is a 3 year degree structured around 12 core units, 8 major specialist subjects and 4 electives drawn from specialisation streams in cyber security, network security, cloud computing, virtualisation, systems administration, network administration, IoT and emerging digital technologies. The course is accredited by the Australian Computer Society (ACS), Australia's professional body for the technology sector.

Box Hill delivers the degree in partnership with Microsoft, AWS and Cisco, with students working in specialist laboratories on industry standard software and hardware. Teaching draws on real world projects and industry standard technologies so students graduate with a portfolio of work they can show future employers, rather than a purely theoretical grounding.

Graduates are expected to be able to apply IT and cyber security principles to complex problems, design and evaluate technology solutions, work independently and in multidisciplinary teams, and communicate technical concepts to non-technical audiences, aimed at roles including cyber security analyst, ICT security specialist, cloud administrator, network administrator, systems administrator and IT consultant. Applicants who have completed the Diploma in Information Technology (ICT50220) are eligible for eight subjects (one year) of credit recognition.
dc599cb7-371c-4709-bcbc-bf8b983b2467.curriculum: 12 core units, 8 major specialist subjects and 4 electives across specialisation streams in cyber security, data analytics and AI, cloud computing and IoT, and software engineering, over 3 years.
dc599cb7-371c-4709-bcbc-bf8b983b2467.admission_requirements: International students must have completed an Australian Year 12 (including Mathematics) or international equivalent with a pass. Box Hill Institute only accepts enrolments from international students who are 18 years of age or above at the time of course commencement.
dc599cb7-371c-4709-bcbc-bf8b983b2467.english_requirements: A minimum IELTS overall score of 6.0 (Academic) with no band less than 5.5, or an approved equivalent test.

fa93324d-c134-4302-892f-59c80ed212b9.name: Bachelor of Music Industry (Major in Performance)
fa93324d-c134-4302-892f-59c80ed212b9.description:
Box Hill Institute's Bachelor of Music Industry, CRICOS 104940B, offers six majors (business, composition, music production, performance, songwriting and audio production) sharing a common core taken in the first two years, which covers the music industry from multiple angles including innovation, creativity and entrepreneurship. Students in the Performance major fill roughly half their remaining coursework with the major itself and choose the rest from a pool of over sixty elective and minor subjects.

In Year 1, Performance students learn foundational music theory and ear training on their instrument, instrumental technique for performance, and ensemble playing skills, alongside a weekly "how music works" lecture series. Year 2 moves into creative artistry through analysis and interpretation of repertoire, instrumental lessons, and applying aural and theoretical knowledge in a weekly performance workshop. Year 3 has students conceive and present their own musical projects, applying advanced aural comprehension, theory, technique and stagecraft in an industry expert led workshop.

Students get access to Box Hill's studio facilities, a licensed 200+ capacity on campus music venue, industry standard writing and production suites, an Artist in Residence program, the on campus Tremorverse Record label, and an Analogue Synth Collection. Box Hill builds in two real exit points: a Diploma in Music Industry after 1 year of full time study, and an Associate Degree in Music Industry after 2 years, both built as separate rows in this database. Graduates are aimed at roles including performer, composer, studio roles, broadcaster and marketing professional.
fa93324d-c134-4302-892f-59c80ed212b9.curriculum: 6 common core units (Years 1 to 2, covering the music industry, innovation, creativity and entrepreneurship), 8 major units in Performance (Year 1 foundational technique and ensemble skills; Year 2 repertoire analysis and interpretation with instrumental lessons; Year 3 advanced performance workshop and own musical projects), and 12 electives from a pool of over sixty subjects. Diploma in Music Industry is a real exit point after 1 year; Associate Degree in Music Industry after 2 years.
fa93324d-c134-4302-892f-59c80ed212b9.admission_requirements: International students must have completed an Australian Year 12 or international equivalent with a pass, plus folio requirements (evidence of music ability via live audition, video/online audition link, or DVD), a supervised musicianship test, and an interview covering career goals, course suitability and relevant industry experience. Box Hill Institute only accepts enrolments from international students who are 18 years of age or above at the time of course commencement.
fa93324d-c134-4302-892f-59c80ed212b9.english_requirements: A minimum IELTS overall score of 6.0 (Academic) with no band less than 5.5, or a minimum TOEFL score of 550 (paper based), 213 (computer based) or 79 (internet based), or an approved equivalent test.

f9c7feea-d1e6-40bd-8198-2c43c2b0c825.name: Diploma of Automotive Technology
f9c7feea-d1e6-40bd-8198-2c43c2b0c825.description:
Box Hill Institute's Diploma of Automotive Technology, CRICOS 091702E, is a 12 unit VET qualification covering vehicle mechanics, electronics, diagnostics and repair techniques across engines, transmissions, brakes and steering, combining theoretical study with hands on practical experience in troubleshooting and problem solving.

The course sits at the top of Box Hill's automotive pathway: international students enter it after completing the Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology and Certificate IV in Automotive Mechanical Diagnosis (or the equivalent), and students who don't yet meet entry requirements can apply for all three as a single package offer. Graduates are prepared for automotive technician, mechanic or automotive management roles, with the course aimed at producing professionals able to keep up with evolving automotive technology, including advanced diagnostics, environmental and business/management skills, and systems analysis.
f9c7feea-d1e6-40bd-8198-2c43c2b0c825.curriculum: 12 units of competency in vehicle mechanics, electronics, diagnostics and repair, covering engines, transmissions, brakes and steering, combining classroom theory with hands on workshop practice.
f9c7feea-d1e6-40bd-8198-2c43c2b0c825.admission_requirements: International students must have successfully completed the Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology and Certificate IV in Automotive Mechanical Diagnosis, or the equivalent. Applicants who do not meet entry requirements can apply for all three courses as a package offer. Box Hill Institute only accepts enrolments from international students who are 18 years of age or above at the time of course commencement.
f9c7feea-d1e6-40bd-8198-2c43c2b0c825.english_requirements: A minimum IELTS overall score of 6.0 (Academic), or an approved equivalent test.

919cd84c-80fc-44d9-9976-d2d792d1a452.name: Diploma of Nursing
919cd84c-80fc-44d9-9976-d2d792d1a452.description:
Box Hill Institute's Diploma of Nursing, CRICOS 112198E, is a 2 year, 25 unit of competency qualification (20 core and 5 elective units) that prepares students to work as an enrolled nurse under the direction and supervision of a registered nurse. The course covers implementing general nursing care, assessing client health and analysing health related information, administering and monitoring medications, and attending to older clients, acute care clients and people with mental health conditions, alongside communication skills and the legal and ethical parameters of nursing practice.

Students complete a minimum of 400 hours of mandatory clinical placement across metropolitan, regional and rural healthcare settings. On successful completion, graduates can apply for registration with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia (NMBA) as an enrolled nurse, working across acute care, chronic care, aged care, rehabilitation, primary health care and mental health settings.
919cd84c-80fc-44d9-9976-d2d792d1a452.curriculum: 25 units of competency (20 core, 5 elective) over 2 years, plus a minimum of 400 hours of mandatory clinical placement in metropolitan, regional and rural healthcare settings.
919cd84c-80fc-44d9-9976-d2d792d1a452.admission_requirements: International students must have completed Year 12 or equivalent (including Mathematics), demonstrate high literacy and numeracy skills, and provide before their first clinical placement: a current clear Working with Children Check, a current clear National Police Record Check (Australia and one from their home country), an up to date immunisation/vaccination record (Health Care Worker Category A, including Diphtheria/Tetanus, Poliomyelitis, MMR, Varicella, Hepatitis B, Mantoux Test and flu vaccine), and a complete COVID-19 vaccination history including boosters. Basic computer skills are also required, and some clinical placement facilities may request educational history and a driver's licence or passport. Box Hill Institute only accepts enrolments from international students who are 18 years of age or above at the time of course commencement.
919cd84c-80fc-44d9-9976-d2d792d1a452.english_requirements: Per AHPRA's English language skills registration standard for nurses and midwives, applicants must meet one of the following from a single test sitting (or, in some cases, 2 sittings within 12 months with minimum per-skill floors): IELTS Academic overall 7.0 with no component below 6.5 (writing) or 7.0 (listening, reading, speaking); OET with a minimum grade B in listening, reading and speaking and C+ in writing; PTE Academic overall 66 with component minimums of 66 (listening, reading, speaking) and 56 (writing); TOEFL iBT total 94 with component minimums of 24 (listening, reading, writing) and 23 (speaking); or Cambridge C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency with a minimum of 185 in listening, reading and speaking and 176 in writing. This is a materially higher, profession-mandated bar than Box Hill's general VET English requirement, reflecting AHPRA's enrolled nurse registration standard rather than a generic institute template.

fb50e30c-fd5b-4861-b75b-ddde873f32bc.name: Diploma of Music Industry
fb50e30c-fd5b-4861-b75b-ddde873f32bc.description:
Box Hill Institute's Diploma of Music Industry is a real, TEQSA accredited award (renewal date 14 December 2027) built as the formal 1 year exit point from the institute's Bachelor of Music Industry, rather than a separately marketed standalone course; Box Hill's own Bachelor of Music Industry (Major in Performance) course page states explicitly: "Diploma in Music Industry is an exit point after 1 year of full time study." There is no separate Diploma of Music Industry marketing page on boxhill.edu.au; its content is the first year of the Bachelor's structure.

The first year covers the Bachelor's common core, which looks at the music industry from multiple angles including innovation, creativity and entrepreneurship, alongside foundational major study (in whichever of the degree's six pillars, business, composition, music production, performance, songwriting or audio production, a student has chosen), plus a first slice of the degree's elective pool of over sixty subjects. Students taking the Performance major spend Year 1 on foundational music theory and ear training, instrumental technique, ensemble playing skills, and a weekly "how music works" lecture series.

Students who take this exit point still have access to Box Hill's studio facilities, its licensed 200+ capacity on campus music venue, industry standard writing and production suites, and its Artist in Residence program during that first year.
fb50e30c-fd5b-4861-b75b-ddde873f32bc.curriculum: The first year of the Bachelor of Music Industry's structure: common core units covering the music industry, innovation, creativity and entrepreneurship, plus Year 1 major study and a first slice of the degree's 60+ subject elective pool. For the Performance major specifically, Year 1 covers foundational music theory and ear training, instrumental technique, and ensemble performance skills.
fb50e30c-fd5b-4861-b75b-ddde873f32bc.admission_requirements: Box Hill Institute's own Bachelor of Music Industry page does not publish separate admission criteria for the 1 year Diploma exit point; entry into the Bachelor of Music Industry itself requires an Australian Year 12 or international equivalent with a pass, folio evidence of music ability (live audition, video/online audition, or DVD), a supervised musicianship test, and an interview. Box Hill Institute only accepts enrolments from international students who are 18 years of age or above at the time of course commencement.
fb50e30c-fd5b-4861-b75b-ddde873f32bc.english_requirements: Box Hill Institute's own Bachelor of Music Industry page does not publish a separate English requirement for the Diploma exit point; the Bachelor's own requirement is a minimum IELTS overall score of 6.0 (Academic) with no band less than 5.5, or a minimum TOEFL score of 550 (paper based), 213 (computer based) or 79 (internet based), or an approved equivalent test.

edb09f9d-065f-4d8d-a31d-e141447515f9.name: Associate Degree of Music Industry
edb09f9d-065f-4d8d-a31d-e141447515f9.description:
Box Hill Institute's Associate Degree of Music Industry is a real, TEQSA accredited award (renewal date 14 December 2027) built as the formal 2 year exit point from the institute's Bachelor of Music Industry, rather than a separately marketed standalone course; Box Hill's own Bachelor of Music Industry (Major in Performance) course page states explicitly: "Associate degree in Music Industry is an exit point after two years of full time study." There is no separate Associate Degree of Music Industry marketing page on boxhill.edu.au; its content is the first two years of the Bachelor's structure.

The first two years cover the Bachelor's full common core (which looks at the music industry from multiple angles including innovation, creativity and entrepreneurship), the first two years of major study in whichever of the degree's six pillars a student has chosen, and a slice of the degree's elective pool of over sixty subjects. Students taking the Performance major spend Year 1 on foundational music theory, ear training, instrumental technique and ensemble skills, then Year 2 stepping toward creative artistry through repertoire analysis and interpretation, instrumental lessons, and a weekly performance workshop applying aural and theoretical knowledge to contemporary repertoire.

Students reaching this exit point have had two years of access to Box Hill's studio facilities, its licensed 200+ capacity on campus music venue, industry standard writing and production suites, its Artist in Residence program, and the on campus Tremorverse Record label.
edb09f9d-065f-4d8d-a31d-e141447515f9.curriculum: The first two years of the Bachelor of Music Industry's structure: common core units covering the music industry, innovation, creativity and entrepreneurship across Years 1 and 2, plus two years of major study and a slice of the degree's 60+ subject elective pool. For the Performance major specifically, this covers foundational technique and ensemble skills in Year 1, then repertoire analysis, interpretation and a weekly performance workshop in Year 2.
edb09f9d-065f-4d8d-a31d-e141447515f9.admission_requirements: Box Hill Institute's own Bachelor of Music Industry page does not publish separate admission criteria for the 2 year Associate Degree exit point; entry into the Bachelor of Music Industry itself requires an Australian Year 12 or international equivalent with a pass, folio evidence of music ability (live audition, video/online audition, or DVD), a supervised musicianship test, and an interview. Box Hill Institute only accepts enrolments from international students who are 18 years of age or above at the time of course commencement.
edb09f9d-065f-4d8d-a31d-e141447515f9.english_requirements: Box Hill Institute's own Bachelor of Music Industry page does not publish a separate English requirement for the Associate Degree exit point; the Bachelor's own requirement is a minimum IELTS overall score of 6.0 (Academic) with no band less than 5.5, or a minimum TOEFL score of 550 (paper based), 213 (computer based) or 79 (internet based), or an approved equivalent test.
